title: Limiting Dilution & Clonal Expansion
author: Synthego
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.srqed5w
materials: Aspirate medium from cells across all conditions.

steps.title: Detach Transfected Cells
steps.instruction: Detach cells from the 24-well plate using a dissociation reagent.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the 24-well plate containing transfected cells from the humidified CO2 incubator to a biological safety cabinet.
Add 250 μl of TrypLE TM (or other appropriate cell dissociation reagent) to the cells, adjusting volumes based on the cell culture vessel size if cells have been passaged.
Incubate the cells for 5 minutes at 37°C and 5% CO2 or until the cells detach.
Transfer the well plate back to the biological safety cabinet.

steps.title: Neutralize and Collect Cells
steps.instruction: Stop the dissociation process and collect the cells into tubes.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of medium (250 μl) to the TrypLE TM in each well to neutralize dissociation.
Pipet 3-4 times (or more if needed) with a 1 ml pipette to break up cell clumps, or pass cells through a cell strainer.
Transfer the cells from each condition to a separate sterile 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Quantify and Prepare Cell Suspension
steps.instruction: Determine cell concentration and prepare the dilution for plating.

substeps.instruction: Count the cells from each condition using a hemocytometer or automated cytometer.
Calculate the cell concentration (cells/ml) in the suspension.
Determine the number of 96-well plates required for each pool (1-2 plates per edited pool are recommended).
Warm medium at 37°C in a water bath.

steps.title: Perform Limiting Dilution
steps.instruction: Dilute cells to a single-cell concentration and dispense into 96-well plates.

substeps.instruction: Dilute cells in a series of 10-fold dilutions to a final concentration of 0.5-1 cells/100 μl of medium (approx. 1 cell/well) or 120 cells in 12 ml of normal growth medium. Scale based on the number of plates (e.g., for 5 x 96-well plates, dilute 600 cells in 60 ml of normal growth medium). Note: concentration can be adjusted between 0.5-5 cells/100 μl.
Transfer the diluted cell suspension to a large sterile reservoir.
Dispense 100 μl/well of the diluted cell suspension to each well using a multichannel pipette.
Repeat this process for each edited population selected for clonal expansion.

steps.title: Incubate and Screen for Colonies
steps.instruction: Incubate plates and monitor for the growth of single-cell colonies.

substeps.instruction: Transfer plates to a humidified incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 and change medium as needed.
Visually screen plates via microscope for established single colonies for approximately two weeks.
Optional: If a clone imager is available, image plates 2-4 hours after plating and again 5-7 days later to confirm single-cell origin.
Mark establishing colonies by circling the well on the lid or recording in a spreadsheet.
When colonies reach 70% confluence, transfer them to a 24-well plate, reserving a portion of cells from each colony for genotyping.

steps.title: Genotype and Validate Clones
steps.instruction: Identify successful knockouts through genetic and functional analysis.

substeps.instruction: Isolate genomic DNA, PCR-amplify the edited region, and perform Sanger sequencing on the amplicons.
Analyze sequence data using Synthego’s Inference of CRISPR edits (ICE) tool to identify wild type, homozygous edits, or heterozygous edits.
Select colonies containing indels that cause frameshift mutations, ideally those generating a premature stop codon.
Maintain a few colonies from Mock or Negative Control conditions as isogenic wild type comparisons.
Split and expand putative knockouts for cryopreservation.
Perform functional validation using immunoblot, ELISA, flow cytometry, or an appropriate activity assay.
